CVE-2026-100407.title: Git for Windows: git-credential-wincred OAuth Store Heap Overflow
CVE-2026-100407.description: Git for Windows is the Windows port of Git. From 2.44.0.windows.1 until 2.55.0.windows.3, the git-credential-wincred store operation in contrib/credential/wincred/git-credential-wincred.c uses _scwprintf() to size a formatted wide-character credential buffer without space for the terminating NUL when both password and oauth_refresh_token are present. The operation also passes a byte count to _snwprintf_s() where a wide-character count is required, allowing the terminator to be written one WCHAR past the heap allocation before CredWriteW() persists the credential. The resulting fixed two-byte NUL overwrite can terminate the helper with Windows heap-corruption status and can cause git credential approve to report success even though the OAuth credential was not stored. This issue is fixed in version 2.55.0.windows.3.

CVE-2026-115878.title: Stanza: RCE via pickle deserialization in the lemmatizer
CVE-2026-115878.description: Stanza is a Stanford NLP Python library for tokenization, sentence segmentation, NER, and parsing of many human languages. From 1.14.0 until 1.15.0, loading an attacker-supplied lemmatizer checkpoint can execute arbitrary code because stanza/models/lemma/trainer.py stores pos_dict as gzip-compressed pickle bytes and Trainer.load passes the decompressed stream to unrestricted pickle.loads. The outer torch.load call uses weights_only=True, but the nested bytes are treated as a primitive and are not inspected by that allowlist. The path is reachable during pipeline construction through a caller-influenced lemma_model_path, before inference begins. This issue is fixed in version 1.15.0.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net: lan966x: restore RX state on reload failure

lan966x_fdma_reload() backs up rx->page_pool and rx->fdma before
reallocating the RX resources for the new MTU. If the allocation fails,
the restore path puts these fields back before restarting RX.

However, the reload path also updates rx->page_order and rx->max_mtu
before calling lan966x_fdma_rx_alloc(). These fields are not restored on
failure, so RX can be restarted with the old pages, old FDMA state and
old page pool, but with the page geometry from the failed new MTU.

page_order while the actual RX pages still come from the old allocation.
For example, after a failed reload to a jumbo MTU, xdp_init_buff() may be
called with a frame size larger than the restored RX pages.

CVE-2026-99145.title: drm/xe: Don't transfer shrinker pages for pinned bos on purgeable state change
CVE-2026-99145.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/xe: Don't transfer shrinker pages for pinned bos on purgeable state change

Pinned bos have their pages removed from the shrinker's shrinkable /
purgeable counts on pin, and added back on unpin according to the
bo's purgeable state at that time.

However, xe_bo_set_purgeable_shrinker() unconditionally transfers
pages between the shrinkable and purgeable counts. If the purgeable
state of a pinned bo changes, for example by userspace madvising
DONTNEED on a VMA of a bo that is also pinned as a scanout buffer,
this underflows one count and, after unpin, leaves the other one
permanently inflated.

Only update the purgeable flag for pinned bos, and leave the page
accounting to unpin.

CVE-2026-99471.title: KVM: PPC: Book3S HV: Add SRCU protection for virtual-mode HPT hcalls
CVE-2026-99471.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

KVM: PPC: Book3S HV: Add SRCU protection for virtual-mode HPT hcalls

The virtual-mode HPT hcall handlers (H_ENTER, H_REMOVE, H_BULK_REMOVE,
H_CLEAR_REF, H_CLEAR_MOD) call into book3s_hv_rm_mmu.c, which accesses
memslots via kvm_memslots_raw(). kvm_memslots_raw() uses
rcu_dereference_raw_check() to bypass SRCU lockdep annotation checking.
This is safe in real mode because the entire guest entry/exit is wrapped
in srcu_read_lock/unlock inside kvmppc_run_core() and
kvmhv_run_single_vcpu().

However, since commit 6165d5dd99db ("KVM: PPC: Book3S HV: add virtual
mode handlers for HPT hcalls and page faults"), these same handlers are
also executed in virtual mode via kvmppc_pseries_do_hcall(), which runs
after SRCU has already been released on guest exit.

A concurrent KVM_SET_USER_MEMORY_REGION deletion or move can therefore
call synchronize_srcu_expedited() — which does not wait for this thread —
and then kfree(slot)…

CVE-2026-99615.title: l2tp: only return sessions of the given tunnel in l2tp_session_get()
CVE-2026-99615.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

l2tp: only return sessions of the given tunnel in l2tp_session_get()

Commit 5f77c18ea556 ("l2tp: use IDR for all session lookups") made
pppol2tp_connect() and the netlink session commands find sessions with
l2tp_session_get(), passing the socket of the tunnel they name.

L2TPv3 session IDs are unique per network namespace, except that
sessions carried over UDP are only unique per UDP socket, the socket of
their tunnel. However, l2tp_v3_session_get() only checks the socket when
another session has the same session ID. Otherwise it returns the
session, whichever tunnel it belongs to. As of now, a session command
that names the wrong tunnel acts on a session of another tunnel, and a
PPPoL2TP socket for a second L2TPv3 tunnel fails with EEXIST, because it
finds session 0 of the first tunnel.

The issue can be reproduced with:

ip l2tp add tunnel tunnel_id 3 peer_tunnel_id 3 encap udp \
local 127.0.0.1 remote 127.0.0.1…
